check.note: Ex14a asks for the common difference of terms containing z. Ex16a says the terms make a linear sequence and asks for k, which means the differences between successive terms must be equal. Both extend the subtract-successive-terms idea to terms with an unknown. The text never states this method, so it is inferred.

Both quotes are in the anchored text. The step 20=4+2n-2 expands 2(n-1), and 520=120+15n-15 expands 15(n-1). A constant times a binomial is distributed as a step in solving for n, which is the multiplication skill in g10m1s6-1-1.
